questions.question: Explain the basic function of options in derivatives.
questions.solution_html:
• Options are derivative contracts that give the buyer the right but not the obligation to buy (Call
  • option) or sell (Put option) an underlying asset at a predetermined strike price on or before
  • a specific date. Their basic functions are hedging (protecting against price risk)
  • speculation (betting on price movements with limited downside), and income generation
  • (writing options for premium). Unlike forwards/futures, there is no obligation to exercise.
questions.final_answer: (writing options for premium). Unlike forwards/futures, there is no obligation to exercise
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List factors affecting beta.
questions.solution_html:
• Financial leverage (debt-equity ratio), Operating leverage (fixed vs variable costs)
  • Business/Industry risk (cyclical vs non-cyclical), Company size and market position
  • Economic conditions and interest-rate sensitivity.
questions.final_answer: Economic conditions and interest-rate sensitivity
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define beta in the CAPM equation.
questions.solution_html:
• Beta (β) is the measure of systematic (market) risk of a security or portfolio relative to the
  • market portfolio. In the CAPM equation: Expected Return = Rf + β (Rm – Rf) β = 1 →
  • moves with market; β > 1 → more volatile; β < 1 → less volatile.
questions.final_answer: moves with market; β > 1 → more volatile; β < 1 → less volatile
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List types of options.
questions.solution_html:
• Call and Put options, American (exercisable any time before expiry) and European
  • (exercisable only on expiry)
questions.final_answer: Call and Put options, American (exercisable any time before expiry) and European
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the parties in a swap contract.
questions.solution_html:
• A swap involves two counterparties who agree to exchange cash flows. In an interest-rate
  • swap, one party (fixed payer) pays a fixed rate and receives a floating rate; the other
  • (floating payer) does the opposite. No principal is exchanged (notional principal only).
  • Parties are typically a bank/financial institution and a corporate client.
questions.final_answer: Parties are typically a bank/financial institution and a corporate client
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is the time frame typically associated with speculation?
questions.solution_html:
• Short-term (days to a few months). Speculators aim to profit from short-term price fluctuations
  • rather than long-term fundamentals.
questions.final_answer: Short-term (days to a few months). Speculators aim to profit from short-term price fluctuations
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List roles of derivatives in portfolios.
questions.solution_html:
• Hedging (risk reduction), Speculation (leveraged bets), Arbitrage (exploiting mispricing)
  • Portfolio insurance / dynamic asset allocation, Enhancing returns / income generation
questions.final_answer: Hedging (risk reduction), Speculation (leveraged bets), Arbitrage (exploiting mispricing)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the slope of the CML.
questions.solution_html:
• The slope of the Capital Market Line (CML) is (E(Rm) – Rf) / σm (market Sharpe ratio). It
  • represents the additional expected return per unit of total risk (standard deviation) for
  • efficient portfolios combining the risk-free asset and market portfolio. Steeper slope =
  • better risk-return trade-off.
questions.final_answer: better risk-return trade-off
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define portfolio manager under SEBI.
questions.solution_html:
• As per SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, a portfolio manager is a body corporate
  • registered with SEBI who, pursuant to a contract or arrangement with a client, advises or
  • directs or undertakes on behalf of the client (whether discretionary or non-discretionary)
  • the management or administration of a portfolio of securities or the funds of the client.
questions.final_answer: the management or administration of a portfolio of securities or the funds of the client
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define variance.
questions.solution_html:
• Variance is a statistical measure of the dispersion of returns around the mean (expected)
  • return. It is the square of standard deviation and quantifies total risk (systematic +
  • unsystematic) of an investment. Formula: σ² = Σ (Ri – R̄ )² / n.
questions.final_answer: unsystematic) of an investment. Formula: σ² = Σ (Ri – R̄ )² / n
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What role does personal financial goals play in selecting investments?
questions.solution_html:
• Personal goals (retirement, education, home purchase, etc.) determine time horizon, risk
  • tolerance, liquidity needs, return requirements, and tax status. They guide asset
  • allocation (e.g., equity for growth, debt for safety) to ensure investments match life-stage
  • objectives.
questions.final_answer: objectives
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is diversification principle?
questions.solution_html:
• Spreading investments across uncorrelated or low-correlated assets/sectors to reduce
  • unsystematic (specific) risk without sacrificing expected return. Core of Modern Portfolio
  • Theory – “Do not put all eggs in one basket.”
questions.final_answer: Theory – “Do not put all eggs in one basket.”
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is the Dow Jones Theory?
questions.solution_html:
• Also known as Dow Theory, it is a technical analysis framework stating that the market
  • moves in three trends (primary, secondary, minor). A primary trend is confirmed only
  • when both the Dow Jones Industrial Average and Transportation Average move in the
  • same direction. The market discounts all known information.
questions.final_answer: same direction. The market discounts all known information
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define portfolio selection.
questions.solution_html:
• The process of choosing the optimal combination of securities that maximises return for
  • a given risk level (or minimises risk for a given return) based on investor objectives, usually
  • using Markowitz’s efficient frontier or other optimisation models.
questions.final_answer: using Markowitz’s efficient frontier or other optimisation models
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is the assumption regarding investor behaviour in CAPM?
questions.solution_html:
• Investors are rational, risk-averse, hold fully diversified portfolios, and care only about
  • expected return and systematic risk (beta). They have homogeneous expectations and
  • can borrow/lend at the risk-free rate.
questions.final_answer: can borrow/lend at the risk-free rate
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Explain the Efficient Market Theory and its three forms.
questions.solution_html:
• Prices reflect all available information → no abnormal returns possible. Weak form: Past
  • price/volume info already reflected. Semi-strong form: All public information reflected.
  • Strong form: All information (public + private) reflected. Implications for
  • technical/fundamental analysis.
questions.final_answer: technical/fundamental analysis
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain portfolio management and wealth management and bring out their / differences.
questions.solution_html:
• Portfolio Management: Focused on securities selection, asset allocation, risk-return
  • optimisation. Wealth Management: Holistic – includes portfolio + tax planning, estate
  • planning, insurance, retirement, philanthropy. Differences (scope, clients, services
  • regulation).
questions.final_answer: regulation)
